name: Fluorine-eating enzyme
subtitle: a designed enzyme that breaks forever chemicals

effects.effect: a learned model predicts a protein's 3D shape from its sequence

effect: a learned model predicts a protein's 3D shape from its sequence
how: PFAS are in the blood of almost everyone, and the only treatments are filters that concentrate the problem into a sludge someone then has to burn at great expense. Nature has a few weak enzymes that snap carbon-fluorine bonds, and a learned model can now propose protein shapes that grip a PFAS chain and hold the bond where the enzyme can hit it. A column packed with such an enzyme would turn a captured sludge back into salt and harmless fragments.
obstacle: Carbon-fluorine is the strongest bond in organic chemistry, and no enzyme yet gets near the rate a treatment plant needs.
why: Design tools are new enough that nobody has yet tried hard at this bond.
real: Protein-language-model design of candidate defluorinases has been attempted (68 candidates, a handful expressed, PFOA activity untested) and a natural HAD-II defluorinase shows modest fluoride release, plus commercial enzyme-design partnerships; no designed enzyme or enzyme column has been shown to defluorinate PFAS in water.
